as_told.title: Carl Jung's flying saucer book and the mandala archetype

plain: In 1958 the Swiss psychiatrist Carl Jung published a book called Flying Saucers: A Modern Myth of Things Seen in the Skies, which looked at why so many people were reporting saucers. Michels raises it in several episodes. In one he says Jung read the saucers as mandalas, the circle that stands in Sanskrit tradition for a complete and whole mind, and in that telling he dates the book only to the 1950s. A researcher named James Madden, talking about the book from his own reading, describes how its argument moves. He says Jung starts out treating the saucers as a rumor that spreads through a crowd. As the book goes on, Madden says, Jung finds them harder to wave away, and by the end he is noting "and yet they're on radar." The tellers raise the book because it suggests that one of the great students of the human mind could not fully explain the sightings as psychology.
